title.purpose: ReportCard headers, page h1s, auth masthead.

micro.purpose: The smallest tracked-caps step: taglines, dt stat labels, badges, HealthBadge's stage word, AuthFrame's edge label — 10px.

data.purpose: Every measured figure: scores, counts, percentages, HealthBadge's score, form input text.

shadows.name: sheet-lift
shadows.purpose: The only shadow in the system — applied to ReportCard and the auth card so they read as a sheet resting on the desk.

components.name: Intake Field
components.description: An underlined blank rather than a bordered box — reads as a form field to fill in.
components.css: .ds-field { display: block; font-family: 'Public Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-field span { display: block; margin-bottom: 6px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.1em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #5b6469; } .ds-field input { width: 100%; border: none; border-bottom: 1px solid #d9dcd6; background: transparent; padding: 8px 0; font-family: 'Courier Prime', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 14px; color: #14181b; } .ds-field input::placeholder { color: #5b6469; } .ds-field input:focus { outline: none; border-bottom-color: #b3241d; } .ds-field input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #b3241d; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Health Badge
components.description: The total health score: a plain bordered square holding the score and a neutral stage word. Always ink — a reading, not a verdict.
components.css: .ds-health-badge { width: 96px; height: 96px; border: 1px solid #d9dcd6; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 4px; } .ds-health-score { font-family: 'Courier Prime', ui-monospace, monospace; font-weight: 700; font-size: 24px; color: #14181b; line-height: 1; } .ds-health-stage { font-family: 'Public Sans', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #5b6469; }

components.description: One reference-range row: label, bracket with a fill-to-reading bar and a tick, value/max in tabular figures. Always ink-muted/ink — never colored by whether the reading is high or low.

narrative.overview:
GitHub Insights reads a profile the way a clinic reads a patient: identity first, then a panel of measured values against stated reference ranges, then a plain total reading. The system rejects the category default — indigo buttons, rounded card grids, a soft-shadowed dashboard — in favor of a printed-document register: hairline rules instead of shadows, tabular monospace figures instead of decorative stat tiles. Nothing here is soft. Corners are near-sharp, borders are 1px, and color is rationed to one accent, used only where the visitor is meant to act — never to grade a reading as good or bad.

Two registers exist by design: a light 'paper' mode (a report sheet on a lit desk) and a dark 'negative' mode (the same report read on a light table in a dark room) — dark mode is not an inverted tint of light mode, it swaps to its own near-black ground and lifted-surface pairing.
keyCharacteristics: Paper-and-ink palette: one accent (stamp red), reserved for actions — never for grading a reading.
Every number is a measurement: tabular monospace figures throughout.
Depth comes from hairline rules and 1px borders, not shadows.
The total health score is a plain bordered readout (HealthBadge) — a measurement alongside the others, not a verdict.

rules.name: The Rationed Ink Rule
rules.body: Stamp Red is the only saturated color in the system, and it marks an action or a locked state — never a reading. It never becomes a background fill larger than a button; everywhere else it appears as text or a 1px rule.

rules.name: The Ungraded Reading Rule
rules.body: A measured value's color never depends on whether the number is high or low. MeasuredValue's fill and tick are always ink-muted/ink; HealthBadge's score and stage word are always ink. A low reading is a fact the report states, not a fault it flags.

rules.name: The Negative Register Rule
rules.body: Dark mode is a second ground truth, not an inverted light theme: ground and surface are independently defined near-black values, and the accent shifts brighter to stay legible against them.

rules.name: The Instrument-Numeral Rule
rules.body: Any number a visitor might compare against another number renders in Courier Prime with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Paper-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth is a hairline border plus a 1px shadow at most. A card, panel, or overlay that needs more separation gets a rule between it and its neighbor, never a heavier shadow.

rules.name: The All-Rectilinear Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the system is circular. An earlier version stamped the total score in a rotated circular ring; that read as a verdict rather than a measurement and was replaced with a plain bordered square (HealthBadge) at the same visual weight.

dos: Do render every measured figure in Courier Prime with tabular figures.
Do keep Stamp Red rationed to actions and locked-content markers; never a large background fill and never a grade on a reading.
Do use a 1px hairline rule for separation and state; a colored border above 1px is a violation.
Do give dark mode its own near-black ground and lifted surface, not an inverted light palette.
Do show locked/gated content as a sealed or redacted document, never a generic blur-plus-CTA.
donts: Don't use rounded-full or soft rounded-xl/2xl cards — the system's one radius is 3px, reserved for ReportCard.
Don't use a unicode glyph as an icon.
Don't add a kicker or eyebrow label above a heading.
Don't color a measured value or the total score by whether it's high or low.
Don't frame the total score as a verdict (a stamp, a pass/fail badge, a colored ring) — it is a plain reading.
Don't reduce ink-muted with an opacity modifier for placeholder or secondary text.
